title: India vs Pakistan Asian Games Final: Predicted XIs, Key Battles, Match Details
excerpt: India and Pakistan meet in the men's cricket gold medal match at the Asian Games 2026 on October 3 in Nisshin, Japan — with India favourites to retain the title after a 124-run semifinal rout of Sri Lanka.
body:
• India face Pakistan in the Asian Games men's cricket final on October 3 at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin, Japan — the first Asian Games final between the arch-rivals.
  • India are unbeaten and favourites after beating Sri Lanka by 124 runs; Ishan Kishan's unbeaten 80 and Jasprit Bumrah's new-ball burst lead the charge.
  • Pakistan reached the final with a rain-shortened chase against Bangladesh, powered by Sufyan Moqim's three wickets and an unbeaten 59-run stand from Abdul Samad and Hasan Nawaz.
  • The match starts at 10:30 AM IST (SonyLIV/Sony Sports in India, PTV Sports in Pakistan); a complete washout would see both sides share the gold.

India will face Pakistan in the men's cricket gold medal match at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, October 3, at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan — the first time the arch-rivals have met in an Asian Games final. India, the defending champions, arrive as heavy favourites after a ruthless 124-run semifinal demolition of Sri Lanka, while Pakistan booked their place with a nervy win over Bangladesh in a rain-reduced contest. According to Cricket Addictor, a complete washout would result in both teams sharing the gold medal rather than any seeding-based tie-break.

Predicted Playing XIs

India (predicted): Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Shreyas Iyer (c), Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah.

Pakistan (predicted): Sahibzada Farhan (c), Saim Ayub, Usman Khan (wk), Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz, Abdul Samad, Arafat Minhas, Ahmed Daniyal, Mohammad Wasim Jr, Abrar Ahmed, Sufyan Moqim.

India are reported to have a fully fit squad, and captain Shreyas Iyer is expected to back the opening pair of Abhishek Sharma and Sooryavanshi, who struck a quick 38 in the semifinal. Pakistan have largely settled on their combination, with Abrar Ahmed and Sufyan Moqim leading a spin-heavy attack on a surface that has increasingly favoured slow bowling as the tournament has progressed, according to reports from CricTracker.

Context & Background

Cricket returned to the Asian Games programme at Hangzhou 2023, where India won the men's gold after the final against Afghanistan was washed out and the medal was awarded on seeding. This time the format has produced a first: an India-Pakistan final for gold. The T20I head-to-head reads decisively in India's favour — 14 wins to Pakistan's 3 across 17 meetings, with India winning the most recent clash in February 2025, according to CricTracker.

The road to the final told two different stories. India posted 169/7 against Sri Lanka after early trouble at 24/2, rebuilt by Ishan Kishan's unbeaten 80 off 46 balls — five sixes and four boundaries — before the bowlers dismissed Sri Lanka for just 45 in 9.4 overs. Bumrah struck twice in the opening over; Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma chipped in alongside several run-outs.

Pakistan's path was messier. In a 13-over semifinal against Bangladesh, their bowlers — led by Moqim's 3 wickets — restricted Bangladesh to 110/8, but the chase wobbled to 53/4 before Abdul Samad (30* off 15) and Hasan Nawaz (27* off 22) carried them home with nine balls to spare.

Impact & Analysis

The pitch is the tactical centrepiece. Korogi Sports Park — a converted baseball ground in Japan's Aichi prefecture — has developed cracks through the tournament, producing uneven bounce and making stroke-play difficult. Batting first looks like the play: 12 of the venue's 20 matches have been won by teams defending totals, with an average first-innings score around 142, per pitch analyses.

"The captain winning the toss could prefer to bat first and put runs on the board in the final."

— Cricket Addictor, Asian Games 2026 final preview

Key battles will decide it: Saim Ayub's powerplay aggression against Bumrah's new-ball threat, the in-form Kishan against the in-form Moqim, and Shreyas Iyer's middle-order anchoring against Abrar Ahmed's variations. India have superior depth — seven bowling options and batting down to number nine — but Pakistan's young spin trio has already handled knockout pressure, and a low-scoring final would narrow the gap significantly.

There is also a weather asterisk. Rain has repeatedly disrupted the latter stages of the tournament, and passing showers remain a concern in Nisshin; the DLS method could enter play if the second innings is interrupted.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, this is the one fixture that needs no marketing. The 10:30 AM IST start translates to 1:00 AM Eastern in the US and Canada — a late night for one of the biggest rivalries in world sport, with live streaming available globally. The SonyLIV stream is expected to draw millions, and diaspora communities in the Gulf, UK, and North America traditionally gather around India-Pakistan clashes in numbers that few other sporting events match.

What's Next

Toss is the first decision point: bat first on a wearing surface is the expected call, and the DLS par-score awareness could shape the second innings if showers intervene. Beyond the gold, the result feeds into selection narratives — performances here count for fringe Indian internationals like Kishan, Samson, and Sooryavanshi. If rain wins out entirely, both anthems play and the gold is shared — an outcome neither side will want.
